metadata.name: Beast Within destroys a permanent, creates a Beast token
metadata.description: p1 casts Beast Within targeting a Sol Ring on p2's battlefield. Sol Ring is destroyed and p2 creates a 3/3 green Beast creature token. Tests Beast Within's dual effect: destroy any permanent + create Beast token for target's controller.
metadata.generation_notes: Beast Within oracle: 'Destroy target permanent. Its controller creates a 3/3 green Beast creature token.' Cost {2}{G}. Targets any permanent — Sol Ring is an artifact permanent. After resolution: Sol Ring goes to p2's graveyard (indestructible check: Sol Ring has no indestructible), p2 gets a 3/3 Beast token. Beast Within goes to p1's graveyard. Initial: p1 has Beast Within with {2}{G} in pool; p2 has Sol Ring on battlefield (untapped). RE-APPROVED 2026-09-05 (LL-1, scutemob-255): the old retirement reason claimed the destroy itself did not resolve and Sol Ring survived. That was stale — the destroy worked; what failed was the token's RECIPIENT. Beast Within's TokenSpec had no `recipient`, so the 3/3 was created for the CASTER (p1) instead of the destroyed permanent's controller (p2), and this script's `zones.battlefield.p2 includes Beast` assertion is exactly the pin for that. Fixed by setting `recipient: PlayerTarget::ControllerOf(DeclaredTarget 0)` on the def plus the CR 608.2h departed-controller fallback in `resolve_player_target_list`.

script.step_note: p1 casts Beast Within targeting p2's Sol Ring.
